title: Concrete Driver Dependency (Lack of Abstraction)
pattern: A high-level business logic struct contains a direct field reference to a concrete, third-party vendor library client instead of an abstract interface.
why_bad: It makes it impossible to switch vendors or mock the dependency during tests. The application's core logic is coupled directly to the chosen database vendor's API.
detection: Direct storage of third-party driver connection/client structs in high-level domain or orchestrator structs.
counterexample: Trivial scripts or short-lived CLI utilities where adaptability is not a concern.
source: Andrew Hunt & David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (2019), Chapter 2 ("Reversibility"); Martin Fowler, *Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture* (2002), Chapter 8 ("Data Mapper").
